title: Call Conductor: Name mapping and compatibility runbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: We continue to see customer confusion and errors when apps migrate between OpenAI-style tool calling and our legacy function invocation surface. Calls fail due to minor name variations, differing parameter shapes, or incomplete provenance when streaming is involved. Call Conductor is a lightweight runtime-layer that harmonizes invocations across contract variants without forcing clients to change immediately. Goals: 1) Provide deterministic name-resolution and a provenance-aware routing layer that maps OpenAI-style tool names and payloads to existing legacy function handlers. 2) Preserve streaming behavior and structured-output fidelity when we translate between tool call formats. 3) Make mappings observable and reversible (telemetry + backfill) so we can roll forward or rollback safely. Scope: runtime shim + migration runbook + fallbacks. Not in scope: schema-level redesign of customer functions or forced-breaking client contracts. This ticket covers design, a PoC implementation in the routing layer, E2E tests, rollout plan (feature flags/canaries), and documentation for SDK teams.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic name-resolution algorithm implemented in the runtime that handles case/char variants, common aliases, and tokenized abbreviations
Structured output produced by translated invocations must match legacy function expectations for a representative set of 10 customer prompts (ref test vectors)
Streaming requests that include tool calls maintain chunk order and rehydration semantics after translation (E2E test coverage)
Telemetry emitted for every translated invocation with resolution reason and confidence score; dashboard linked in Console
Rollback path: feature-flagged translation can be disabled without dropping in-flight requests and with metric-level verification
tasks: Spike: implement name fingerprinting and similarity score (2d)
Design RFC: Call Conductor policies (priority: routing, alias table, conflict resolution) and publish for review
Runtime: add translation hook to request router and header X-Invocation-Provenance
E2E: create 10 canonical test vectors covering streaming + structured outputs
Telemetry: add events call_conductor.resolve and call_conductor.fallback with tags
SDK: update open-source JS shim README with migration steps and opt-in flag
Rollout: canary in dedicated, monitor error-rate, latency, and wrong-resolution-rate dashboard
Docs: runbook for on-call with reproducible replay steps and revert checklist

notes: Design trade-offs: - Conservative initial policy will bias towards legacy function handlers to avoid behavioral regressions. - Long-term plan: configurable policy per-organization so high-migration customers can opt into 'aggressive aliasing'. - Streaming complexity: translation layer must be stream-aware and attach minimal provenance metadata to KV cache entries to avoid token misalignment. - We avoid adding per-request heavyweight schema conversion; instead we support a small set of canonical mappers and a fallback raw payload pass-through. Monitoring: we will track wrong-resolution-rate and map it to automated backfill jobs if we see >0.5% across production traffic. Migration checklist in runbook will include pre-rollout audit, canary, customer opt-in, and final cutover steps.
